## Introduction

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/)

In this post, I will look at how body mass varies across penguin species and sex, using the 'palmerpenguins' daatset. 

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()
```

# Examining the data

```{python}
penguins = penguins.dropna()
penguins.head()
```

# Summary statistics

```{python}
#| label: tbl-mass-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Mean body mass (g) by species and sex."

mass_summary = (
    penguins.groupby(['species', 'sex'])['body_mass_g'].mean().reset_index()
)
mass_summary
```

## Visualising body mass by species

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body mass of penguins by species" 

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

species_colors = {
    "Adelie": "tab:blue",
    "Chinstrap": "tab:orange",
    "Gentoo": "tab:green",
}

for species, group in penguins.groupby("species"):
    ax.scatter(
        group["flipper_length_mm"],
        group["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7,
        color=species_colors[species],
    )

ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Species")
plt.show()
```

## Findings

Adelie and Chinstrap have similar findings, where they have both smaller body mass and smaller flipper length. Gentoo, however, has both a large body mass and large flipper length.
